optimized_sql:
WITH
date_d1 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy = 4 AND d_year = 1999
),
date_d2 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10 AND d_year = 1999
),
date_d3 AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10 AND d_year = 1999
),
store_sales_filtered AS (
    SELECT ss_sold_date_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_customer_sk, ss_ticket_number, ss_net_profit
    FROM store_sales
    WHERE ss_sold_date_sk IN (SELECT d_date_sk FROM date_d1)
),
store_returns_filtered AS (
    SELECT sr_customer_sk, sr_item_sk, sr_ticket_number, sr_net_loss
    FROM store_returns
    WHERE sr_returned_date_sk IN (SELECT d_date_sk FROM date_d2)
),
catalog_sales_filtered AS (
    SELECT cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_net_profit
    FROM catalog_sales
    WHERE cs_sold_date_sk IN (SELECT d_date_sk FROM date_d3)
),
sales_returns_bridge AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT
        sr.sr_customer_sk,
        sr.sr_item_sk,
        ss.ss_store_sk,
        ss.ss_item_sk AS i_item_sk,
        max(ss.ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
        max(sr.sr_net_loss) AS store_returns_loss
    FROM store_sales_filtered ss
    JOIN store_returns_filtered sr
        ON ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
        AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
        AND ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
    GROUP BY sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_item_sk, ss.ss_store_sk, ss.ss_item_sk
),
catalog_profit AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT
        cs.cs_bill_customer_sk,
        cs.cs_item_sk,
        max(cs.cs_net_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
    FROM catalog_sales_filtered cs
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM sales_returns_bridge b
        WHERE b.sr_customer_sk = cs.cs_bill_customer_sk
          AND b.sr_item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
    )
    GROUP BY cs.cs_bill_customer_sk, cs.cs_item_sk
)
SELECT
    i.i_item_id,
    i.i_item_desc,
    s.s_store_id,
    s.s_store_name,
    max(b.store_sales_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
    max(b.store_returns_loss) AS store_returns_loss,
    max(c.catalog_sales_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM sales_returns_bridge b
JOIN catalog_profit c
    ON b.sr_customer_sk = c.cs_bill_customer_sk
    AND b.sr_item_sk = c.cs_item_sk
JOIN item i
    ON b.i_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
JOIN store s
    ON b.ss_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
GROUP BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
LIMIT 100

1. PRE-AGGREGATE CATALOG_SALES — TARGET: catalog_sales ↔ store_returns join on `sr_customer_sk = cs_bill_customer_sk` and `sr_item_sk = cs_item_sk` — TRANSFORMATION: Filter catalog_sales by d3 (1999, months 4–10), semi-join it to the qualifying store-return customer/item pairs, aggregate `max(cs_net_profit)` per `(cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_item_sk)`, and use this compact aggregate instead of raw catalog_sales to eliminate the store-return × catalog-order fan-out.

2. PRE-AGGREGATE STORE_SALES ⋈ STORE_RETURNS — TARGET: store_sales/store_returns join on `(ss_customer_sk=sr_customer_sk, ss_item_sk=sr_item_sk, ss_ticket_number=sr_ticket_number)` — TRANSFORMATION: After applying d1/d2 filters, join the two store facts on their natural key and aggregate immediately by `(sr_customer_sk, sr_item_sk, s_store_sk, i_item_sk)` with `max(ss_net_profit)` and `max(sr_net_loss)`, producing a compact bridge relation for the catalog_sales join.

3. MATERIALIZE THE AGGREGATED CTES — TARGET: the returned-sales bridge and the per-customer/item catalog_sales aggregate — TRANSFORMATION: Force materialization of these intermediate relations so each is scanned once and reused for both the semi-join filtering and the final grouping, avoiding repeated evaluation of the heavy fact-table reductions.

4. DEFER ITEM/STORE DISPLAY COLUMNS — TARGET: `i_item_id`, `i_item_desc`, `s_store_id`, `s_store_name` in GROUP BY/ORDER BY — TRANSFORMATION: Carry only `i_item_sk` and `s_store_sk` through the heavy joins and aggregations; join item and store to add the text labels and group/order by them only in the final small result step, reducing hash/sort key width.

5. USE DATE-RANGE SEMI-JOINS ON FACT DATE KEYS — TARGET: `ss_sold_date_sk`, `sr_returned_date_sk`, `cs_sold_date_sk` with d1/d2/d3 — TRANSFORMATION: Restrict each fact table to the exact date_dim window via `IN`/semi-join (d1: April 1999; d2/d3: months 4–10 of 1999) before the multi-fact joins, so each fact scan starts from its filtered date subset rather than relying on later join-time filtering.
